Theme

Household, washing & chores

curtain noun

also curtains, open the curtains, draw the curtains

classical

Traupman 123
Traupman 300

aulaeum, aulaeī n.

noun, second declension

curtain, hanging or drapery

Plural aulaea, aulaeōrum n. pl., curtains (Traupman 123).

Other words

  • vēlum, vēlī n. — a curtain (on a window or shower), awning

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 300

  • cortīna, cortīnae f. — Traupman’s “curtain”

    noun, first declension · avoid · modern · Traupman 123: curtains, aulaea, cortīnae

    Classically a round cauldron, and the tripod of Apollo (Lewis & Short); use aulaeum or vēlum.

Examples

  • aulaea dīdūcere / obdūcere

    open / draw the curtainscomposed

  • Sed aulaeīs dīductīs nec arborēs nec montem nec lūmina vīdit

    But when he opened the curtains he saw neither the trees nor the mountain nor the lightscomposed

  • Pater igitur, aulaeīs obductīs lūmineque exstīnctō, puerum amplexus, dē Arīone narrāvit

    So Dad drew the curtains, turned off the light, put his arm round the boy and told him about Arioncomposed

  • vēla obdūcere

    to draw the curtainsTraupman 300

See also curtain rod, curtain ring, curtain track, shower curtain.
